you’re kidding! phrase

also you’re kidding, don’t kid me, are you kidding?, you must be joking, you’re pulling my leg, no kidding

classical

Hor. S. 2.5.58: an prūdēns lūdis mē obscūra canendō? (Lewis & Short), s.v. furō
Traupman 101
Traupman 336

Lūdis mē.

lūdō with the person as object: “you are playing with me”

you’re making fun of me, you’re kidding

Other words

  • Nē mē lūdās! — don’t kid me!

    nē with the present subjunctive, a prohibition · also used · classical · Plaut. Curc. 326: vidē nē mē lūdās, mind you’re not kidding me; Traupman 101; Traupman 336

    In comedy; in prose a prohibition prefers nē with the perfect subjunctive or nōlī with the infinitive.

  • Jocāris. — you’re joking

    also used · classical · Plaut. Most. 1081: sciō, jocāris nunc tū, I know, you’re joking now; Traupman 101: jocāris nunc tū

See also joke, make fun of, really?.

SourcesLewis & Short: ludo · Lewis & Short: jocor

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 101, 336.
